Synopsis:
Fed Governor Lisa Cook's attorney formally rebutted the Trump White House's mortgage fraud allegations used to justify her removal, calling them legally insufficient and politically motivated. Cook's lawyer argues any mortgage paperwork errors were inadvertent and partly lender-caused, and notes Trump himself signed similar documents. The legal battle continues in lower courts following a 5-4 Supreme Court ruling blocking her removal. The broader context is Trump's sustained effort to reshape the Fed board to favor lower interest rates, targeting Biden-appointed governors after ceasing pressure on new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.
